;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**The [[Taliban]] claims responsibility for an attack on Sunday on an [[Afghan military]] centre in southern [[Helmand Province|Helmand]] where they say that "dozens were killed or wounded". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-taliban-attacks/taliban-attack-military-centre-in-afghanistan-casualties-reported-idUSKBN22G0FU?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Ituri conflict]]
**The [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|armed forces]] of the [[Democratic Republic of Congo]] announce that 12 soldiers were killed in an attack by militants in [[Ituri Province]] over the weekend. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/12-killed-in-attack-on-dr-congo-army-base/1829071 (Anadolu Agency)]
*[[Macuto Bay raid]]
**[[President of Venezuela|Venezuelan President]] [[Nicolás Maduro]] says "13 [[Terrorism|terrorists]]", including two [[United States|U.S.]] citizens working for [[Jordan Goudreau]]'s private security company Silvercorp USA, have been detained after foiling a plot to [[assassinate]] him, accusing them of "playing [[John Rambo|Rambo]]". [[State television]] broadcasts footage of captured mercenaries in [[Aragua]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-venezuela-security/us-veteran-behind-failed-venezuela-plot-says-two-american-mercenaries-detained-idUKKBN22G2O6 (Reuters)]
**Opposition leader [[Juan Guaidó]] denies any involvement with the Silvercorp USA operation. Jordan Goudreau claims his company signed a contract with Guaidó to remove Nicolás Maduro from power by force, but says he has only been paid "a tiny share of the amount agreed upon." [https://www.toledoblade.com/news/World/2020/05/04/venezuela-guaido-denies-invasion-link/stories/20200505045 (AP via ''Toledo Blade'')]

;Arts and culture
*[[2020 Pulitzer Prize]]
**[[Reuters]] wins the 2020 [[Pulitzer Prize for Breaking News Photography]] for its coverage of the [[2019–20 Hong Kong protests|protests]] in [[Hong Kong]]. [https://www.reuters.com/news/picture/reuters-wins-pulitzer-prize-for-breaking-idUSRTX7H87E (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*[[Coronavirus recession]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
**The [[Federal government of the United States|U.S. government]] announces plans to borrow [[United States dollar|$]]3 trillion for the second quarter, five times more than the previous record set during the [[Financial crisis of 2007–08|2008 financial crisis]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-52537938 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
***[[Prime Minister of Japan|Prime Minister]] [[Shinzo Abe]] extends the national [[state of emergency]] to May 31. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-japan/japans-abe-extends-state-of-emergency-to-may-31-idUSKBN22G05T (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
*** New Zealand reports no new cases of COVID-19 for the first day in almost two months. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/may/04/new-zealand-records-first-day-with-no-new-covid-19-cases-since-before-lockdown (''The Guardian'')]

;Law and crime 
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Colorado]]
**A [[Colorado]] man who organized planned armed protests against the state’s stay-at-home orders is arrested after pipe bombs were discovered at his house. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/colorado-man-planning-armed-protest-states-coronavirus-restrictions/story?id=70491370 (ABC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Department for International Trade|UK Trade Minister]] [[Conor Burns]] resigns after a watchdog group recommended suspending him from [[Parliament of the United Kingdom|parliament]] for making "veiled threats" towards a company his father had financial disputes with. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-52531078 (BBC News)]

;Science and technology
*A team of [[United Kingdom|British]] and [[Kenya]]n scientists announce the discovery of Microsporidia MB, a [[parasite|parasitic]] microbe in the [[Microsporidia]] fungi group that blocks [[mosquito]]s from carrying [[malaria]]. While acknowledging they need to understand how the microbe spreads and how it blocks the disease, the team believes it has potential to be used in malaria control. [https://www.bbc.com/news/health-52530828 (BBC News)] [https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-16121-y (''Nature'')]
*A previously undetected [[Apollo asteroid|Apollo group]] [[asteroid]] [[2020 JJ]] passes 4,350 miles (7,000 kilometres) away from [[Earth]]. It is the closest [[near-Earth object]] since [[2019 UN13]]. [https://www.cnet.com/news/asteroid-sneaks-past-satellites-in-one-of-the-closest-flybys-on-record/ (CNET)]
